questions.subject: US_GOVERNMENT
questions.topic: A licence requirement and a claimed liberty

stimulus.body: Fixing a common mistake: a student claims any licence requirement violates liberty. Neutral licences are generally upheld.

questions.stem: Is the student right?
questions.explanation: Neutral licence requirements are generally upheld. All-licences or profit views misstate the balance.
questions.hint: Do all licences violate liberty?

questions.subject: US_GOVERNMENT
questions.topic: A liberty of parents over their children's schooling
questions.stem: Fixing a common mistake: stage one, parents choose a school. Stage two, is the choice protected?

options.text: Yes, by parental liberty in education
No, only public schools are allowed

questions.explanation: Parental liberty in education protects school choice. State-decision or speech views misstate the source.
questions.hint: Which liberty covers parental choice?

questions.subject: US_GOVERNMENT
questions.topic: What a hearing before deprivation must include
questions.stem: Fixing a common mistake: a student says a hearing must be a full trial; is that right?

options.text: Yes, a full trial is required
Yes, if the interest is large
No, notice and a chance to respond suffice

questions.explanation: A hearing requires notice and a chance to respond, not necessarily a full trial. Overstating or denying misstates due process.
questions.hint: Must a hearing be a full trial?

questions.subject: US_GOVERNMENT
questions.topic: How much process is owed before a deprivation
questions.stem: Fixing a common mistake: a student asks whether the same process is owed in every deprivation case.

answer.exemplar: No, the process owed varies by balancing the private interest, risk of error, and government interest under Mathews.

questions.explanation: The process owed varies by case under Mathews. One-size-fits-all misstates the balancing.
questions.hint: Is the process the same in every case?

questions.subject: US_GOVERNMENT
questions.topic: Termination of an entitlement with no prior hearing

stimulus.body: Fixing a common mistake: a student says an entitlement can never be terminated without a prior hearing. Post-deprivation process may suffice.

questions.stem: Is the student right?

options.text: Yes, a prior hearing is always required
Yes, if the entitlement is large
No, no hearing is ever needed

questions.explanation: Post-deprivation process may suffice in some cases. Always-prior or never-needed views misstate due process.
questions.hint: Is a prior hearing always required?

questions.subject: US_GOVERNMENT
questions.topic: What equal protection forbids and does not require

stimulus.body: Fixing a common mistake: a student claims equal protection requires identical treatment in all cases. It forbids unjustified unequal treatment.

questions.stem: Is the student right?

options.text: No, it forbids unjustified unequal treatment
No, it requires no treatment at all

questions.explanation: Equal protection forbids unjustified unequal treatment, not identical treatment in all cases. Overstating or narrowing misstates it.
questions.hint: Does equal protection require identical treatment?

questions.subject: US_GOVERNMENT
questions.topic: A neutral permit requirement and its group effect
questions.stem: Fixing a common mistake: stage one, a neutral permit rule affects one group more. Stage two, does that alone violate equal protection?

options.text: No, only intent matters in all contexts
Yes, any disparate impact violates it
Yes, if the group is large
No, disparate impact alone is not enough

questions.explanation: Disparate impact alone does not violate equal protection without discriminatory intent. Overstating impact or intent misstates the standard.
questions.hint: Is disparate impact alone enough?
